agency: Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection, Office of Oil and Gas Management
basis: permit date (the day DEP issued the well's drilling permit)
cadence: daily (the layer is current to a day or two)
name: Pennsylvania
note: Permits to drill a well, by the day DEP issued them (the layer has one row per well). Permits that expired unused or whose well the operator reported not drilled stay in the count: DEP issued them. Most are gas wells, many of them shale wells. Storage, injection, disposal and observation wells are their own band, a handful in six years. Re-drills, deepenings, alterations and changes of use are authorizations on existing wells that the layer does not show, so those bands are not told. The layer holds a few percent fewer wells than DEP's weekly Workload Report counts as permitted (555 against 576 for January 1 to October 23, 2026). The fluid is DEP's well type; an undetermined type or a dry hole is unknown.
